narration: Why was there ice in there at all? The Moon barely tilts on its axis. So the floors of some polar craters never see the Sun.
visual_brief: Sunlight sweeping over polar terrain while crater floors stay in shadow.

candidates.title: Highlighting Plumes
candidates.description: At least four distinct plumes of water ice spew out from the south polar region of Saturn moon Enceladus in this dramatically illuminated image. Light reflected off Saturn is illuminating the surface of the moon while the sun backlights the plumes.

candidates.title: Dark Side of the Moon: Enceladus
candidates.description: Enceladus looks as though it is half lit by sunlight in this view from NASA's Cassini spacecraft, but looks can be deceiving.
